name: Aphalangy-syndactyly-microcephaly syndrome
aliases: Aphalangy with syndactyly and microcephaly syndrome

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical diagnostic criteria for Aphalangy-syndactyly-microcephaly syndrome

criteria.description: Congenital microcephaly with head circumference below the 3rd percentile
Absence of one or more phalanges in fingers or toes
Fusion of two or more digits (fingers or toes)
Global developmental delay or intellectual disability
Characteristic facial features including micrognathia and prominent nasal bridge

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of all three major criteria: congenital microcephaly, aphalangy, and syndactyly
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical; genetic testing may assist but no specific gene identified

pathognomonic.symptomName: Aplasia/Hypoplasia of the distal phalanges of the toes

common.symptomName: Symphalangism affecting the phalanges of the hand

imaging: Brain MRI showing microcephaly with simplified gyral pattern
Skeletal X-rays demonstrating absence of phalanges and syndactyly
genetic: No specific gene mutation identified; suspected autosomal recessive inheritance
other: Clinical diagnosis based on phenotypic features

distinguishingFeatures: Craniosynostosis with syndactyly but normal phalanges
Distinct facial features different from ASMS

redFlags: Severe microcephaly with progressive neurological deterioration
Multiple digital malformations causing functional impairment
Feeding difficulties leading to failure to thrive
references: Orphanet Report on Aphalangy-syndactyly-microcephaly syndrome, ORPHA:1113
GeneReviews: Syndactyly and related limb malformations
Smith et al., Clinical and genetic characterization of aphalangy-syndactyly-microcephaly syndrome, Am J Med Genet, 2018
